title: Ferroptosis and Lipid Metabolic Dysregulation Are Associated With Periodontitis and Peri‐Implantitis Complicated by Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross‐Sectional Study
html:
ABSTRACT

Objective

Although the clinical associations between T2DM and periodontal or peri-implant diseases have garnered widespread attention, metabolomic studies decoding the specific local metabolic alterations within these comorbid conditions remain scarce. This study aimed to apply untargeted metabolomics to elucidate the potential metabolic signatures of T2DM in periodontitis and peri-implantitis.

Materials and Methods

Thirty patients were enrolled in this non-target metabolomics study. Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and peri-implant crevicular fluid (PICF) samples were collected and analyzed. It further investigates the commonalities and heterogeneity in metabolic profiles between T2DM with periodontitis (T2DM-P) and T2DM with peri-implantitis (T2DM-PI). Furthermore, mitochondrial ultrastructure was evaluated via transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and select differential metabolites were cross-validated utilizing immunofluorescence (IF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC).

Results

Our data indicate that T2DM is associated with lipid metabolism dysregulation. In the T2DM-P group, C8 and C10 showed exploratory signals of altered acylcarnitine metabolism. Moreover, γ-GGC and 13-HPOT in the T2DM-PI group and L-cystine in the T2DM-P group were identified as potential candidate metabolites. However, these findings did not remain statistically significant after FDR correction and should be interpreted cautiously. Integrating these metabolomic findings with our experimental findings from TEM, IF, and IHC suggests that cellular ferroptosis emerges as a potential common pathway linked to T2DM-related oral tissue destruction.

Conclusion

This study not only reveals the potential metabolic signatures of T2DM-P and T2DM-PI but also highlights the underlying involvement of ferroptosis. Nonetheless, these exploratory findings require rigorous empirical validation for future clinical interventions.
